## Your own price source: Nord Pool or ENTSO-e prices in the forecast

If you already run Nord Pool (built into Home Assistant or from HACS) or
ENTSO-e, the integration can now take the day-ahead prices from there. They
replace the forecast for every hour your source already knows, and our
forecast carries on after that.

- **Usually earlier, in every market.** The exchange prices we pass on come
  from freely licensed sources, and those can be hours late - on 20 November
  the German day was missing altogether. Nord Pool and ENTSO-e usually have
  tomorrow's prices shortly after the midday auction. The plans, the current
  price and the retail formula use them within seconds of reaching your
  source, without waiting for our next update.
- **Real prices where we may not publish them.** In 18 zones - NO1, NO3-NO5,
  SE1, SE2, FI, RO, SK, GR, BG, GB and the six Italian zones other than ITN -
  we may only pass on our forecast. With your own source you see the real
  prices for today and tomorrow there too.
- **Your prices stay with you.** They are read inside Home Assistant only and
  never sent to our API or anywhere else.

**Setting it up:** set Nord Pool or ENTSO-e to the bare exchange price (no
VAT, no additional costs), then open **Settings > Devices & services >
Energy Price Forecast EU > Configure** and pick the sensor. With ENTSO-e
that is **Average electricity price**.

Why the bare price: VAT and grid charges belong in this integration's retail
formula, so they reach the forecast days too. Your source only knows today
and tomorrow. The dialog checks this when you save and says what to change
if the sensor looks like it carries VAT or charges, or uses another currency.

[How it works, units and limits](https://github.com/BackupBaTTerY/energypriceforecast-home-assistant/blob/main/docs/own-price-source.md)

**After updating, restart Home Assistant.** Reloading the integration is not
enough. Nothing changes until you pick a source.

## A README that is easier to find your way in

The README now opens with a three-step quick start and a table that sends
you to the right section for what you want to do. A new section,
[Using it with an AI assistant](https://github.com/BackupBaTTerY/energypriceforecast-home-assistant#using-it-with-an-ai-assistant),
has a block of facts to paste into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Assist, and
prompts that write an automation for your device, turn your price sheet
into the retail formula, or explain a diagnostics file.

## Tell us how it works for you

This has been tested against the code of all three integrations, not yet in
many real homes. A line in
[Discussions](https://github.com/BackupBaTTerY/energypriceforecast-home-assistant/discussions)
on which source you use, and whether the prices line up, helps a lot.
